author: reek
body: The three voices are rendered together, one output sample at a time, because ring modulation and hard sync couple a voice to its neighbour: voice 0 is modulated by voice 2, voice 1 by voice 0, voice 2 by voice 1. All per-voice runtime state -- phase accumulator, packed envelope, noise LFSR -- plus the two filter integrators live in a 44-byte state block (sid-rt), threaded through the sample loop by mutation. sid-render allocates and resets a fresh block for a self-contained one-shot tone; sid-render-stream takes a caller-owned block so an emulator can keep the oscillators and envelopes running continuously across frame boundaries.

author: reek
body: Render one output sample. The three oscillators advance together so that hard sync and ring modulation can read each other's phase, then each voice's waveform is scaled by its envelope, the routed voices are summed into the state-variable filter, and the filtered and unfiltered sums are scaled by the master volume, clamped, and written as one 16-bit stereo frame. Every mutation lands in the sid-rt state block, so the next sample resumes exactly where this one left off.
